data.narrative:
Helion is a Series F frontier-technology company in the Climate & Energy sector, having raised over $1 billion to date. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers in the same sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, a narrow peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting quality thresholds.

The stage-progression method was the applicable triangulation approach. Starting from the last post-money valuation of $5.4B, applying a typical Series F-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.3x yields an implied valuation of $7.0B. This method reflects the expected step-up in valuation associated with progression from Series F financing. No peer-median approach could be reliably applied, as the broader Climate & Energy peer set of eight companies did not yield three or more data points within sufficiently narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier), making a cross-peer comparison uninformative.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6.0B to $8.1B, with a central estimate of $7.0B. The current stated valuation of $15.5B sits substantially above this implied range. Key uncertainties include market conditions affecting downstream financing rounds, technology risk inherent to frontier-energy companies, and the limited applicability of comparable-company analysis within this specialized sector. The narrow peer dataset constrains confidence in cross-sectional validation.
